Question
========

Which of the following statements about data frames is correct?

Answerlist
----------

* A data frame is a special kind of list, where each slot holds an equal-length vector.
* A data frame is a special kind of matrix that allows the data types to differ between columns.
* A data frame and a matrix are the same underlying object type, just printed differently.
* A data frame is a special kind of list, where each slot must hold a length-one vector.
* A data frame has nothing in common with either lists or matrices. It's a completely separate object type.
* A data frame is a special kind of vector, where each element holds and equal-length character vector.

Solution
========

A data frame is implemented as a list, where every list slot contains a vector-like object, with the added constraint
that all of those vectors must have equal length. This is structure allows us to view data frames as a "rectangular,"
table-like structure while still being a list underneath. Data frames are *not* matrices. Matrices are generalizations
of atomic vectors that require every element to share the same type, while data frames are special lists that allow each
column to have its own type.
